description: First five minutes. The job of an opener is to get the guest speaking in concrete, specific detail before they settle into the version of themselves they brought to be interviewed. Specificity is the lever: 'yesterday' beats 'a typical day' every time.

questions.text: Walk me through yesterday. Not a typical day - yesterday specifically, from the moment you started working.
questions.lands_because: Nobody has a rehearsed answer for a specific day. It produces texture, names, and small problems - which is the raw material for every follow-up in the episode.
followups: What was the hardest twenty minutes of that?
Was that a normal day or were you dealing with something unusual?

questions.text: What is the first thing you look at when you start work?
questions.lands_because: Every profession has an instrument panel - a board, a queue, a chart, a market, a forecast. Naming it hands the audience the guest's frame of reference in one sentence.
followups: What are you hoping not to see there?

questions.text: If I shadowed you for a week, what would surprise me most?
questions.lands_because: Invites the guest to compare their reality against a civilian's expectation, which is exactly the gap the episode exists to close.
followups: Is that surprising to people inside your field too, or just outsiders?

questions.text: What did you do this week that nobody outside your field would even recognize as work?
questions.lands_because: Surfaces the unglamorous substrate of the job early, and signals to the guest that you are interested in the real thing rather than the highlight reel.
followups: How much of the job is that?

questions.text: How do you describe your job to someone inside your field, versus how you describe it at a party?
questions.lands_because: The distance between the two answers is usually the whole story, and the guest gets to be funny about it. Low risk, high yield.
followups: Which one is closer to true?

questions.text: What is a tool you touch every single day that most people have never heard of?
questions.lands_because: Objects and systems are easy to talk about and hard to be evasive about. Works equally for a torque wrench, a claims platform, a mixing desk, or a scheduling system.
followups: Is it good? Would you design it differently?
What did people use before it?

questions.text: What time of year is hardest in your world, and what happens then?
questions.lands_because: Nearly every profession has a crunch - harvest, close, Q4, testing season, storm season, camp, deployment workup. Asking about it shows you know work has a calendar.
followups: What does the rest of your life look like during that stretch?

questions.text: When you meet someone else who does what you do, what do you ask them?
questions.lands_because: Hands you the insider question for free. Often the best question of the interview is the one they just told you they ask.
followups: Ask me nothing - just tell me what a good answer to that sounds like.
